# An instance built at run time reads and writes page state, and a test reads
# a computed of it, on every target.
#
# android's test build holds the page's state in a class MainScreen is handed,
# and `chooser`, a composable of its own under the `if`, spelled
# `state.picked` with no `state` in reach: the file now holds the state the
# test made, which each new one replaces. A test's read of `shown`, which the
# composable remembers as a derived value, called it as a function. And
# `choose`, a function of `chooser` writing the page's state, was made a member
# of the state class, where `count` is not.

sngl test --platform=none app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'
sngl test --platform=html app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'
sngl test --platform=bubbletea --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'
sngl test --platform=fyne --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'
sngl test --platform=gtk4 --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'
sngl test --platform=android --language=kotlin app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'

-- app.sngl --
import ui "sngl:ui"
import test "sngl:test"

var picked = "a"

component chooser ui.node {
    var count = 0

    func shown() => "picked {picked}"

    // Counts the pick and makes it, from the composable's state and the page's.
    func choose() {
        count += 1
        picked = "b"
    }

    ui.button #pick(text=shown(), @click { choose() })
}

component main ui.node {
    var away = false

    ui.button #leave(text="leave", @click { away = !away })
    if !away {
        chooser #c
    }
}

func testComesBack(t test.Test, c main) {
    if c.c != null {
        c.c.pick.click()
    }
    c.leave.click()
    t.assert(c.c == null)
    c.leave.click()
    t.assert(c.c != null && c.c.shown() == "picked b")
}
